journalRanking.policy: Never infer journal or article strata from impact factor, publisher, reputation, or LLM output. Record a classification only with scheme, level, evaluation area, cycle, ISSN or DOI, retrieval date, and an official scheme source. Journal classification is not article-level evidence quality.

curationPolicy.claimReview: Every included claim is a candidate for a second human review against the linked article and locator. None is accepted for decision support.

records.title: Butler-Volmer-Monod model for describing bio-anode polarization curves
records.summary: The authors formulate bio-anode kinetics by coupling enzyme-kinetic substrate conversion with Butler-Volmer electron transfer. This is a candidate formulation reference, not calibration or validation of METREV.
records.provenanceNote: Curator-added bibliographic candidate; study applicability and the quoted abstract locator require independent human review before use.

claims.content: The paper formulates bio-anode kinetics by combining an enzyme-kinetic representation of biochemical conversion with Butler-Volmer electron-transfer kinetics.
claims.sourceSnippet: A kinetic model of the bio-anode was developed based on a simple representation of the underlying biochemical conversions.
claims.analystNote: Candidate summary; independently verify the complete abstract and the parameter assumptions. This paper does not validate METREV.

records.title: Modelling and simulation of two-chamber microbial fuel cell
records.summary: A two-chamber MFC model combines biochemical reactions, Butler-Volmer expressions, and mass/charge balances to represent steady and dynamic behaviour in the study's setup.
records.provenanceNote: Curator-added bibliographic candidate; scope, equations, and any experimental comparison require independent human review before use.

claims.content: The study describes a two-chamber MFC model that combines biochemical reactions, Butler-Volmer expressions, and mass and charge balances for steady and dynamic behaviour.
claims.sourceSnippet: A MFC model based on a two-chamber configuration is developed that simulates both steady and dynamic behaviour.
claims.analystNote: Candidate summary; independently verify the full paper and model comparison conditions. This paper does not validate METREV.

records.title: Multi-Population Model of a Microbial Electrolysis Cell
records.summary: The paper presents a dynamic MEC model with multiple microbial populations. Its reported conditions and validation boundary must be checked before translating the structure to another case.
records.provenanceNote: Curator-added bibliographic candidate; author list and study conditions require independent human verification.

claims.content: The article presents a dynamic microbial electrolysis cell model with multiple microbial populations.
claims.sourceSnippet: This work presents a multi-population dynamic model of a microbial electrolysis cell (MEC).
claims.analystNote: Candidate abstract claim; verify model structure, calibration data, and independent validation before treating reported performance as predictive evidence.

records.title: Hydrogen production by Geobacter species and a mixed consortium in a microbial electrolysis cell
records.summary: The study compares hydrogen production and recovery for Geobacter species and a mixed consortium in MECs; recovered product depends on microbial and electrical operating conditions.
records.provenanceNote: Curator-added candidate checked against the journal and PubMed records; quantitative operating details remain to be independently reviewed.

claims.content: The study compares hydrogen production and recovery in MECs using hydrogen-utilizing and non-hydrogen-utilizing Geobacter species and a mixed consortium.
claims.sourceSnippet: A hydrogen utilizing exoelectrogenic bacterium (Geobacter sulfurreducens) was compared to both a nonhydrogen oxidizer (Geobacter metallireducens).
claims.analystNote: Correct publication metadata: Call, Wagner and Logan (2009), AEM 75(24), 7579–7587. Keep gross production and gas recovery distinct; independently verify before decision use.

records.title: Microbial fuel cell biosensor for the determination of biochemical oxygen demand of wastewater samples containing readily and slowly biodegradable organics
records.summary: The authors test a single-chamber air-cathode MFC as a BOD biosensor on real wastewater containing slowly biodegradable and suspended organic matter, using integrated charge and voltage response.
records.provenanceNote: Curator-added candidate checked against PubMed, PMC, and the publisher page; confirm license/version and reported error conditions before use.

claims.content: The study applies single-chamber air-cathode MFCs to BOD measurement in real wastewater with suspended or slowly biodegradable organic content.
claims.sourceSnippet: Single-chamber air cathode microbial fuel cells were applied as biosensors for biochemical oxygen demand measurement of real wastewaters.
claims.analystNote: Candidate abstract claim; preserve the batch assay, integrated charge, sample preparation, and reference BOD method before judging transfer to another sensor.

records.title: On Site Evaluation of a Tubular Microbial Fuel Cell Using an Anion Exchange Membrane for Sewage Water Treatment
records.summary: The study evaluates a tubular AEM MFC in sewage-water treatment onsite. Geometry and module-position observations are architectural evidence, not validation of a spatial METREV model.
records.provenanceNote: Curator-added candidate checked against the Frontiers article page; details and issue date should be confirmed during human review.

claims.content: The paper evaluates a tubular anion-exchange-membrane MFC configuration for sewage-water treatment under onsite conditions.
claims.sourceSnippet: This study evaluated the performance of a tubular microbial fuel cell.
claims.analystNote: Candidate architecture claim; check module geometry, HRT, load, and vertical-position observations. Does not validate METREV or support extrapolation to a 0D stack.

records.title: Resilience of anodic biofilm in microbial fuel cell biosensor for BOD monitoring of urban wastewater
records.summary: The study uses MFC biosensors to assess BOD in complex artificial and untreated urban wastewater, making matrix and biofilm adaptation relevant when assessing transferability.
records.provenanceNote: Curator-added candidate checked against Nature and institutional records; methods, matrix, and the scope of the biofilm-resilience result require human review.

claims.content: The study assesses MFC-based BOD biosensors in complex artificial wastewater and untreated urban wastewater.
claims.sourceSnippet: 3D-printed MFC-based biosensors were employed to assess the BOD of sterile complex artificial wastewater and untreated urban wastewater.
claims.analystNote: Candidate abstract claim; verify biofilm history, sample pairing, reference method, and whether results generalize beyond the reported matrices.

records.title: No re-calibration required? Stability of a bioelectrochemical sensor for biodegradable organic matter over 800 days
records.summary: The work assesses calibration stability during more than 800 days of MFC-sensor operation and conditions the no-recalibration interpretation on regular maximum-current normalization.
records.provenanceNote: Curator-added candidate checked against PubMed and the paper record; the calibration protocol and scope require independent human review.

claims.content: The authors studied batch- and flow-mode MFC sensor calibration over more than 800 days and tied the no-recalibration result to regular maximum-current normalization.
claims.sourceSnippet: The aim of this study was to determine the stability of MFC sensor calibrations under fixed conditions over long-term operation.
claims.analystNote: Candidate abstract claim; preserve the normalization and operating-condition caveats. Do not generalize a headline claim to other assays or field cases.

records.title: Domestic wastewater treatment and power generation in continuous flow air-cathode stacked microbial fuel cell: Effect of series and parallel configuration
records.summary: The study compares individual, series, and parallel connection of 40 air-cathode MFC units treating domestic wastewater in continuous flow. It documents an architecture and condition-specific outcomes; it does not establish a universally best topology or validate METREV.
records.provenanceNote: Bibliographic metadata and abstract checked against PubMed (PMID 29529583). The full study design, operating conditions, and transferability require independent human review.

claims.content: Under the reported continuous-flow domestic-wastewater setup with 40 air-cathode MFC units, the study compares unconnected, series, and parallel configurations.
claims.sourceSnippet: A continuous flow stack consisting of 40 individual air-cathode MFC units
claims.analystNote: Candidate architecture claim; verify hydraulic/electrical coupling, wastewater conditions, and scale before transferring the reported outcomes. No topology is assumed universally optimal.

records.title: Model based evaluation of the effect of pH and electrode geometry on microbial fuel cell performance
records.summary: The model couples time-dependent anodic-liquid balances to a two-dimensional biofilm and resolves spatial pH and solute behavior. It is a reference for a research-only spatial profile, not evidence that METREV implements or validates a spatial solver.
records.provenanceNote: Bibliographic metadata and abstract checked against PubMed (PMID 19523880). The spatial formulation, scope, and implementation implications require independent human review.

claims.content: The proposed MFC model couples time-dependent anodic-liquid balances to a two-dimensional biofilm model and calculates spatial pH and solute behavior.
claims.sourceSnippet: a micro-scale individual-based two-dimensional biofilm model
claims.analystNote: Candidate formulation claim. Keep the spatial model separate from METREV’s lumped 0D solver; verify equations, boundary conditions, and reported tests before any implementation work.
